terms.meaning: A business owned and run by one person, who takes all profit and all loss.
Two or more people sharing the profits of a business run by all or any of them for all.
The written, stamped agreement signed by all partners, with the firm's terms.
A family firm of male members descended from a common ancestor, found only in India.
The eldest member who manages a Hindu undivided family business; his liability is unlimited.

items.name: Four kinds of business organisation
items.formula: Private sector, public sector, joint sector and public utilities.
items.example: Small private ones: sole trading, partnership and Hindu undivided family.

items.name: Merits of sole trading
items.formula: No legal formalities, own capital, direct contact with customers.
items.example: The owner keeps all the profit.

items.name: Demerits of sole trading
items.formula: Limited capital and skill; one person bears all losses.
items.example: It may close on the owner's death or insolvency.

items.name: Partnership Act
items.formula: Passed in 1932; section 4 defines a partnership.
items.example: Up to 10 partners in financial business, 20 in general business.

items.name: Active and sleeping partners
items.formula: Active: put in capital and run the business. Sleeping: put in capital but don't take part.
items.example: Both share profit and loss by their capital.

items.name: Nominal and minor partners
items.formula: Nominal: no capital, no work, no profit, but liable for losses. Minor: under 18, gets profit but not losses.
items.example: A minor can join only by all partners' agreement.

items.name: Merits of partnership
items.formula: Easy to form, more capital, division of work, losses shared.
items.example: It can be dissolved with fourteen days' notice.

items.name: Demerits of partnership
items.formula: Disputes, unlimited liability, little stability, shares hard to transfer.
items.example: A partner's death or insolvency may end the firm.

items.name: Registering a partnership
items.formula: Optional; done with the Registrar of Firms, who issues a Certificate of Registration.
items.example: Only a registered firm can sue third parties for loans above Rs. 100.

items.name: Who has a birth right in HUF property
items.formula: Male members of three successive generations after the holder: sons, grandsons and great grandsons.
items.example: Other members' liability is limited to their share.

mistakes.text: Registering a partnership is not compulsory; sole trading concerns can't be registered at all.
A nominal partner gets no profit but is still liable for losses.
The partner limit is 10 for financial (banking) business and 20 for general business.
